newsitem.title: USA: SEC to survey shareholder proposal process.
newsitem.headline: SEC to survey shareholder proposal process.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday it is proposing to revamp the current shareholder proposal process and is seeking fresh ideas from shareholders, companies and other participants in the industry.

"Everything is on the table, we are look for new ideas, including those that could fundamentally change the way we administer the shareholder proposal process," SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt said in a statement.

The regulatory agency distributed a 22-page questionnaire to gather information and opinions from the industry. The results will be used in an analysis of the current rule to be submitted to Congress by Oct 11 as required by the securities reform bill.
"We need input from the parties to see if we can improve the process for everyone," Levitt said.
The survey will ask companies and shareholders about their experiences in the shareholder proposal process and solicit suggestions for revisions to the process.
Some of the suggestions the agency is seeking include alternatives to simplify the process and open companies' proxy materials to a wider range of shareholder proposals.

The shareholder proposal process governs shareholders proposals and under this rule, those eligible investors may submit proposals containing issues to be voted on at the next annual or special meeting of shareholders.
The regulation provides guidelines for submitting proposals, as well as ground rules on which a company may decline to put a proposal to a vote.
The questionnaire is currently available in paper format. The questionnaire must be in the hands of the SEC no later than March 31.
The Securities and Exchange Commission oversees disclosure of information about companies to investors.
